core.title: Produce every user/system flow artifact before it is consumed
core.given: A user/system flow whose participant product capabilities pass artifacts between them
core.when: The planner authors or changes the user/system flow's steps, artifacts or participants, or changes artifact definitions in a participating product capability's manifest
core.then: Every artifact in the user/system flow's flow must be produced before it is consumed.
prefer: Name every flowing artifact as {domain}:{resource} matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*$ — domain starts with a lowercase letter then lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; resource starts with a lowercase letter then lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens.
Define every flowing artifact in participant product capability manifests.
Order the flow so an artifact's producer comes before its consumers.
avoid: Consuming an artifact before it has been produced.
Referencing an artifact that is not defined in participant product capability manifests.
Artifact names that do not match {domain}:{resource} (e.g. uppercase, no colon separator, leading digit, characters outside the allowed sets).
core.why: Artifacts are what flows between user/system flow participants, so each must exist (be produced) before use and be defined where the participating product capabilities declare them.
evidence: Walking the user/system flow's flow in order shows every consumed artifact was produced before it is consumed.
Every artifact referenced in the user/system flow is defined in participant product capability manifests.
verification: The check resolves every artifact in the user/system flow's flow: it verifies each artifact identifier against the {domain}:{resource} pattern, walks the flow in order to verify each artifact is produced before it is consumed, and cross-references the manifests of the product capabilities participating in the user/system flow to verify each referenced artifact is defined there.

The change and finding triggers require observers that do not exist yet: a diff-level observer over user/system flow step lists and over the manifests of product capabilities that participate in some user/system flow (cross-file resolution of participation), and a detector that resolves produce/consume order and cross-references participant product capability manifests.

Which files count as user/system flow definitions and product capability manifests (by kind and location among the stack's plan artifacts) is profile data (the stack's plan-artifact kinds); the rule does not judge files whose kind is neither.

Scope: only user/system flows and the product capabilities participating in them are checked; product capability manifests of non-participating product capabilities, and prose or acceptance edits that change neither a user/system flow's steps/participants nor a participating product capability's artifact definitions, are out of scope.

values: user/system flow step artifact added, renamed or reordered
user/system flow participant added or removed
artifact definition added, renamed or removed in a product capability manifest that participates in a user/system flow
artifact not defined in participant product capability manifests

fires: A planner adds a user/system flow step that consumes an artifact before it has been produced.
A planner adds a user/system flow step referencing an artifact that is not defined in participant product capability manifests.
A planner removes or renames an artifact definition in a participating product capability's manifest while a user/system flow still references it.
A planner names a user/system flow artifact without the {domain}:{resource} form.
doesNotFire: Editing a product capability manifest whose product capability participates in no user/system flow.
Editing prose docs or acceptances that change neither a user/system flow's steps/participants nor a participating product capability's artifact definitions.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds by which the stack identifies user/system flow definition files and product capability manifest files (by kind/location among its plan artifacts); the core's file_kind activation fact and the manifest cross-reference resolve to these kinds.

neutralityNotes: User/system flows, product capabilities, product capability manifests, artifacts and the {domain}:{resource} identifier grammar are ATDD planning-model concepts shared by every stack that adopts this convention (the profile vocabulary itself carries capability/user-system-flow/desired-outcome shapes), so they stay in the core; the only stack-dependent inputs are the concrete plan-artifact kinds that identify user/system flow definitions and product capability manifests (profileRequirements: roles.plan_artifact.kinds). The identifier pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*$ is kept in the core verbatim because it is the convention's own data grammar, identical in the source and the Bun rewrite — the urn profile group covers artifact URNs (component, acceptance, user/system flow, desired outcome, ...), not this rule's flowing-artifact identifiers, so no profile key fits and none was proposed. bun.json's `unless` is empty, so core.unless is empty and there are no unless items to classify. The activation fact notes (observer/detector needs) are carried in core.verification rather than in the fact entries, matching the core schema; the only bunOnly content is the project-specific sample identifiers in verifier_detail[2].
